Subject: EchoThera activation: sales → CS handoff, API quotas, and kickoff cadence

Hi team — looping everyone in for a formal handoff. Quick context: EchoThera (early-stage telehealth platform) signed last week, committed to Redwood Dedicated (2x A100 equivalent) with a go-live target of June 10. Contract signed (SaaS + Dedicated) — see attached SOW_v1. Key things for CS/Implementation to own:

- Primary goal: Production inference for triage assistant and clinician summarization by June 10.
- Expected baseline traffic: ~120 concurrent sessions during business hours; token volume estimated 15M/month (pre-batching).
- API quota ask: they want an initial burst capacity for first 4 weeks (see mutual-action-plan.xlsx) — sales committed to short-term burst during onboarding.
- Security/residency: EchoThera requires logs stored in US region, and a short SOC 2 checklist was attached during procurement.
- Network: they will need IP allowlist and a list of firewall rules for Dedicated endpoints (network_firewall_req.xlsx).

Internal asks:
1) Can CS confirm an implementation owner and a tentative SOW/engagement cadence?
2) Marissa — can you review the API quota/burst ask and outline any service constraints?
3) Priya/John — please confirm preferred kickoff window (we proposed May 4–6) and any blackout dates for your infra team.

I'll keep monitoring; happy to jump on a short triage call if helpful.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
attachments: EchoThera_SOW_v1.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 13:05:00 -0700
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: EchoThera activation: sales → CS handoff, API quotas, and kickoff cadence

Quick technical notes from my side after a pass through the SOW and mutual-action-plan.xlsx:

- Burst capacity: Dedicated pool can support a 2x burst for up to 30 days if we pre-warm the KV caches and reserve node buffers. We will need an explicit order for "onboarding burst" to allocate extra nodes; lead time ~72 hours. This will show up as a separate capacity charge unless we absorb via one-time credit (sales).

- Autoscaling & tail latency: For conversational summarization, token-per-request variability is high. Recommend a conservative concurrency cap for the first 2 weeks and a strict logging sample rate (10%) to keep observability cost manageable.

- Staging topology: We'll need: staging cluster (isolated), preprod cluster that mirrors prod network rules, and a runbook for KV cache warm-up sequence. Provide us with a representative prompt set (~50 interactions) and a few long-context examples to validate cache behavior.

- Security/keys: We require that EchoThera share an API key rotation owner and a service account for S3 access (if they plan to push training/embeddings snapshots). Also confirm whether they require HSM-backed key management (if yes, that's additional procurement).

- IP allowlist: please provide target IPs and expected outbound connections. If EchoThera requires inbound IPs to be static, we'll publish a short list and request a maintenance window for updates.

I'll assemble a short engineering checklist and attach it to the onboarding timeline. For the burst pricing impact, Aditya — can you loop in finance/sales ops if we want to cover the one-time allocations?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Implementation Engineer
Redwood Inference
attachments: engineering_preflight_checklist.md

Thanks for the clear summary — excited to get started. A few notes from EchoThera infra and procurement: 

- Kickoff window: May 5 (preferred) or May 6 (backup). Both dates work for our infra and product teams.
- Staging data: we'll provide a scrubbed sample dataset (50 patient-like sessions) and a representative prompt set by Apr 22.
- API keys & rotation: John will be the owner for key rotation (jmulligan@echothera.com). He will need instructions for rotation and an initial staging token.
- Burst: We accepted the 30-day onboarding burst in principle; procurement is asking for a brief credit to offset initial usage spikes — happy to sign an amendment if needed.
- Legal: we've routed the SOW_v1 to legal; expect counters to be minimal but might include a small NDA addendum around preprod data handling.

One operational ask: can Redwood provide the runbook for KV cache warm-up and a short checklist for verifying latency targets? That will help our infra signoff.

We'll be ready for the intake call on May 5 at 10:00 AM PT if that works.

Thanks,
Priya Rao
